chapter: CBS, return to Ellington and retirement
title: Earlier trombone sections: Tizol, Tricky Sam, Claude Jones
summary: He recalls Sandy Williams, Claude Jones, Wilbur De Paris and his own vacations.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: But that was all after you had left the band. Uh-huh. How about the trombone players before that time. We didn't talk about the -- we talked about the trombone section when you first joined the band.
But then when it became the -- what?
One of the first or the first three-trombone section in the country, which is what somebody has said in a book.
I don't recollect them being the first, but there weren't too many bands that had three trombones.
So, then it was Tricky Sam and Juan Tizol and you.

And then that stayed constant with the exception of a brief time -- somebody named Sandy Williams seems to have played for a couple of months. You were -- were you not in the band at the end of '42, the beginning of '43? That's what it says here.
Well, I would take vacations quite often, so I didn't -- I don't know who came in. And I really don't remember the exact times that I was out, but I would be out a month or so most every year.
And then when Tizol left at the end -- no, early in '44 was when Claude Jones came in.
Claude Jones was a -- wasn't he related to Butter, a cousin or something?
No. No. He was -- he had played in the Kinney's Cotton Pickers when Quentin Jackson played in there.
Wilbur was there also. It was quite a while.
